extracted.intended_audience: San Diego residents, potential supporters, freelance journalists, and prospective interns
extracted.subtask_description: An organization 'About Us' page describing Voice of San Diego’s mission, values, funding and content policies, guidance for freelancers and interns, and contact points for membership and tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — investigative journalism and civic participation
rubrics_metrics.description: To consistently deliver ground-breaking investigative journalism for the San Diego region. To increase civic participation by giving residents the knowledge and in-depth analysis necessary to become advocates for good government and social progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VOSD’s work should be focused on producing ground-breaking investigative reports and providing analysis that equips residents to engage in civic debate and advocacy. The site encourages readers to 'raise your voice by becoming a member.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial independence / Funding policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The donors, sponsors, grantmakers, partners, board members and thousands of individuals who support this service financially do not influence day-to-day coverage, stories or investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a 501(c)(3) nonprofit fully funded by individual members, major charitable gifts, foundations and community partnerships, VOSD depends on contributions but maintains editorial independence. The board of directors sets the operation’s budget, determines the CEO and keeps the organization focused on its mission; staff and board continually review priorities and broad areas of editorial focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding sources and options
rubrics_metrics.description: We are fully funded by individual members, major charitable gifts, foundations and community partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested supporters can become a member or learn about corporate funding options including sponsorships and underwriting. Contributions are necessary to continue the mission; see financial statements for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content sharing policy — open sharing with restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice of San Diego openly shares its staff-produced content with community organizations and publications. But there are some restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community organizations and publications may reuse VOSD content under the terms described in the content sharing guidelines (link provided on the page). Users should check the guidelines for permitted reuse and restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freelance pitch criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: We love to hear from local journalists with ideas brewing. If you have one that fits into our scope of coverage, shoot Managing Editor Andrea Lopez Villafaña a note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freelance pitches should come from local journalists and must fit VOSD’s scope of coverage. The page provides the specific contact (Managing Editor) for pitching; prospective freelancers should tailor pitches to the outlet’s civic/investigative focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internship program requirements and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: We make a point of offering a worthwhile internship to college journalism students and recent graduates interested in real newsroom experience. You’ll tackle a narrative of your own while contributing regularly to our online content. You won’t be making copies or getting us coffee. Plus, we pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are due March 15 for Summer, August 1 for Fall, and December 1 for Winter internships. Applicants should send a cover letter, resume and three clips via email to VOSD_HR@voiceofsandiego.org. Interns are expected to produce original narrative reporting and contribute to online content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and inclusion commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2020, Voice’s staff and board established our first official strategic plan for the organization and incorporated diversity and inclusion goals — including ensuring our staff and sources better reflect the community we serve — into it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With help from readers and experts, VOSD will hold itself accountable to improve every year. The page points to further information about perspectives and commitments to newsroom and content diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational roles and governance (board responsibilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The board of directors sets the operation’s budget, determines the CEO and keeps the organization focused on its mission to do investigative journalism and help residents get the information they need to become advocates for good government and social progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board oversight is presented as the governance mechanism ensuring mission focus and protecting editorial independence; staff and board review priorities and broad editorial focus on an ongoing basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement and values — different newsroom approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Our approach is a little different than traditional newsrooms. Most important, VOSD gives concerned residents the tools to engage in important conversations about their community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VOSD emphasizes building a community of educated San Diegans who ask tough questions and demand answers; the site links to a values page describing how their approach differs from traditional newsrooms and how readers can participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical contact points — membership and news tips
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership inquiries: membership@voiceofsandiego.org. News tips: tips@voiceofsandiego.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page supplies explicit emails for submitting membership questions and news tips, indicating how readers can participate and contribute information to the newsroom.
